findings.claim: Removing the `case <= byte.MaxValue` (Str8) branch in the string header writer changes wire bytes: strings of 32..255 UTF-8 bytes now fall through to the Str16 case (0xDA + 2-byte length) instead of Str8 (0xD9 + 1-byte length). Output grows by 1 byte and differs from all previous versions. It also breaks the MessagePack spec's compact-encoding behavior, and any user who hashes, snapshots or compares serialized bytes will notice. This has nothing to do with the analyzer/SuppressSourceGeneration requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a string of 100 ASCII chars (and one of 32 and one of 255 bytes) with MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<string> on base and head builds. Base starts with 0xD9 0x64; head starts with 0xDA 0x00 0x64. Also run the MessagePackWriter.WriteString and MessagePackPrimitives.TryWriteStringHeader tests.

findings.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys now drops members whose key kind mismatches from the collected members. Previously such a member fell through and was added (or threw on a duplicate key). The generated formatter for types with mixed keys changes, so the output differs from before. Mixed-key types already raise an error diagnostic (MsgPack006), but the generated source and the resulting builds may differ.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests on a [MessagePackObject] type mixing [Key(0)] and [Key("a")] members. Compare the generated formatter on base vs head and check the member set and the diagnostics.

findings.claim: The duplicate-key guards silently skip a member with a duplicate key. Previously `Add` threw ArgumentException, which was swallowed or crashed the generator. Now the generated formatter omits the duplicate member. For a type with duplicate keys the generated output changes. This is only compatible if the duplicate-key diagnostic (MsgPack006) is reliably reported.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a type with two members sharing [Key(0)]. Assert the duplicate-key diagnostic is still reported exactly once and the generator does not throw. Compare the generated output on base vs head.
